title: Vector Databases as a Product Category: Visual Guide
outline: Title: Vector Databases as a Product Category: Visual Guide

1. From Pipeline To Product | the six-stage chunk-and-embed pipeline you already built, with a toggle for whether the index is a derived projection or the only copy | the vector store is a rebuildable serving projection of an authoritative corpus, and every stage gains a version field so a generation can be rebuilt and reconciled

2. Probing IVF Lists | an nprobe slider over 10,000 coarse clusters, switchable between balanced lists and lists after distribution drift | nprobe=20 of 10,000 lists probes about 0.2 percent of clusters, but drift makes the crowded lists near the query far larger so the same knob scans much more and still misses neighbours

3. Five Index Profiles | six workload constraints toggled against HNSW, IVF, IVF-PQ, disk-oriented graph and flat exact, each row showing a FITS/CAUTION/POOR verdict and its reason | an index is chosen by its operational profile — memory, deletion, filtering, training, recovery — not by benchmark recall, and a base index plus a small mutable delta is the shape that dodges several constraints at once

4. Sync Without Dual Writes | five change classes and two transports, with buttons to redeliver an event or deliver a stale version | commit to the source first and project asynchronously so redelivery is harmless and stale versions are rejected, because a dual-write failure is not unlikely so much as undetectable, and revocation needs a stricter objective than freshness

5. Exact Search First | a collection-size and dimension calculator feeding a six-rung ladder of alternatives from precomputed neighbours up to ANN | 100,000 vectors of dimension 384 is 38.4 million scalars and about 154 MB in fp32, so size the exact baseline before buying the operational surface of a vector database
